```{r setup}
#| include: false
source(here::here("R", "area_report_helpers.R"))
source(here::here("R", "area_tiers.R"))
SX   <- readRDS(here::here("data", "area_sussex.rds"))            # R/17_area_analysis.R
DE   <- readRDS(here::here("data", "district_effects.rds"))       # R/18_district_effects.R
D <- bind_rows(lapply(names(DISTRICTS), function(la) tibble(lad = DISTRICTS[[la]], la = la)))
XD <- setNames(lapply(D$lad, function(d) readRDS(here::here("data", paste0("area_", slugify(d), ".rds")))), D$lad)

latest <- SX$latest_panel; latest_lab <- sub("-", "/", latest)
abs_last <- tail(SX$abs_years, 1); abs_prev <- tail(SX$abs_years, 2)[1]
NAT <- SX$national
D <- D |> mutate(doc = district_doc(lad, HAND_WRITTEN),
                 link = sprintf("<a href=\"%s\">%s</a>", doc, lad),
                 md = sprintf("[%s](%s)", lad, doc))

prof <- SX$lad_profiles |> filter(year_label == latest)
rk <- function(lad, col, dir = -1) sapply(lad, function(l) district_rank(SX$lad_profiles, latest, l, col, dir)$r)
n_rank <- district_rank(SX$lad_profiles, latest, "Crawley", "att8")$n

dec <- bind_rows(lapply(D$lad, function(d) XD[[d]]$decomp |> filter(la == d)))
d_tot <- function(l, g) { x <- dec |> filter(la == l, group == g) |> slice(1); x$la_att8 - x$nat_att8 }
d_get <- function(l, g, comp) dec$points[dec$la == l & dec$group == g & dec$component == comp]

ser <- bind_rows(lapply(D$lad, function(d) XD[[d]]$abs_series |> filter(area == d)),
                 SX$abs_series |> filter(area %in% c("England", "East Sussex", "West Sussex")))
s_at <- function(a, tp, col = "abs_rate") sapply(a, function(x) ser[[col]][ser$area == x & ser$time_period == tp])
rs <- bind_rows(lapply(D$lad, function(d) XD[[d]]$reasons |> filter(area == d)),
                SX$reasons |> filter(area == "England")) |>
  filter(time_period == abs_last)
r_at <- function(a, r) sapply(a, function(x) rs$pp[rs$area == x & rs$reason == r])
exa <- bind_rows(lapply(D$lad, function(d) XD[[d]]$excl$area |> filter(la_name == d)),
                 SX$excl$area |> filter(la_name == "England"))
ex_last <- max(exa$time_period)
ex_at <- function(a) sapply(a, function(x) exa$susp_rate[exa$la_name == x & exa$time_period == ex_last])
excess <- sapply(D$lad, function(d) XD[[d]]$area_excess$excess)

fe <- DE$focus |> filter(lad %in% D$lad)
sig_txt <- function(l, s) fe |> filter(lad == l, spec == s, sig) |>
  mutate(t = sprintf("%s (%s%%)", effect_word(outcome), sgn(pct(effect)))) |> pull(t)
dva <- DE$sussex_va |> filter(lad %in% D$lad) |> group_by(lad) |>
  summarise(below = sum(va < 0), va = mean(va), schools = n(), .groups = "drop")

TAB <- D |>
  left_join(prof |> select(lad, schools, att8, att8_dis, gap, fsm, absence, ks2_c), by = "lad") |>
  left_join(dva |> select(lad, va, below), by = "lad") |>
  mutate(r_att8 = rk(lad, "att8"), r_dis = rk(lad, "att8_dis"), r_gap = rk(lad, "gap"),
         u_all = sapply(lad, d_get, g = "All pupils", comp = "Unexplained (school residual)"),
         u_dis = sapply(lad, d_get, g = "Disadvantaged", comp = "Unexplained (school residual)"),
         abs_now = s_at(lad, abs_last), abs_before = s_at(lad, abs_prev),
         excess = excess[lad], reduced = r_at(lad, "Reduced timetable"),
         illness = r_at(lad, "Illness"), susp = ex_at(lad))
```

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
## Draft for discussion

This summary sits beneath the [Sussex review](sussex_review.html) and
the [East Sussex](east_sussex.html) and [West Sussex](west_sussex.html)
documents. Each district also has a document of its own, linked below.
Every figure comes from published Department for Education data and the
national models of
[How to Pull the Right Lever](https://adamdennett.github.io/school_attainment_tool/pulling_the_right_lever_v2.html).
Nothing uses pupil-level records.
:::

# Summary {.unnumbered}

East and West Sussex have twelve districts between them, with
`r sum(TAB$schools)` state-funded secondary schools. Brighton and Hove,
a unitary authority, has no districts and is covered by the Lever report
and the [Sussex review](sussex_review.html).

```{r summary-points}
#| include: false
top <- TAB |> arrange(r_att8); dis_low <- TAB |> arrange(desc(r_dis))
gap_w <- TAB |> arrange(r_gap)
pub <- fe |> filter(spec == "Published specification", sig) |> distinct(lad) |> pull(lad)
sch <- fe |> filter(spec == "With a school term", sig) |> distinct(lad) |> pull(lad)
```

- **Results range widely.** `r top$lad[1]` (`r ord(top$r_att8[1])` of
  `r n_rank` districts in England) and `r top$lad[2]`
  (`r ord(top$r_att8[2])`) are among the strongest in England;
  `r top$lad[nrow(top)]` (`r ord(top$r_att8[nrow(top)])`) and
  `r top$lad[nrow(top) - 1]` (`r ord(top$r_att8[nrow(top) - 1])`) among
  the weakest.
- **Disadvantaged pupils are below England's average in
  `r sum(TAB$att8_dis < NAT$att8_dis)` of the twelve districts.** The
  widest gaps between them and other pupils are in
  `r and_list(head(gap_w$lad, 3))``r if (all(head(gap_w$fsm, 3) < NAT$fsm)) ", all less disadvantaged than England" else ""`.
- **Few district effects survive.** `r and_list(pub)` differ from the rest
  of their county on the published model. Once each school's own record
  is counted, `r if (length(sch)) paste("only", and_list(sch), ifelse(length(sch) == 1, "still does", "still do")) else "none does"`.
  Almost everywhere, what looks like a district difference belongs to
  particular schools.
- **Absence fell in `r sum(TAB$abs_now < TAB$abs_before)` of the twelve
  districts** between autumn and spring `r yr(abs_prev)` and
  `r yr(abs_last)`, and rose or held in
  `r and_list(TAB$lad[TAB$abs_now >= TAB$abs_before])`. Over 2021/22 to
  2024/25, the schools of `r and_list(TAB$lad[TAB$excess > 1])` ran more
  than a point above what their intakes predict.
- **Practice differs more than intake.** Suspensions run from
  `r pp(min(TAB$susp))` to `r pp(max(TAB$susp))` per 100 pupils
  (England `r pp(ex_at("England"))`), and reduced timetables from
  `r pp(min(TAB$reduced), 2)`% to `r pp(max(TAB$reduced), 2)`% of
  sessions (England `r pp(r_at("England", "Reduced timetable"), 2)`%).

# The tiers of this analysis

The Sussex documents are in three tiers:

- **Sussex**: the [Sussex review](sussex_review.html), the region as one
  system.
- **The upper tier**: the three authorities that run schools.
  [East Sussex](east_sussex.html), [West Sussex](west_sussex.html), and
  Brighton and Hove, which is the subject of
  [How to Pull the Right Lever](https://adamdennett.github.io/school_attainment_tool/pulling_the_right_lever_v2.html).
- **The lower tier**: the districts of East and West Sussex, one document
  each, and this summary.

```{r district-links}
#| results: asis
for (la in names(DISTRICTS)) {
  d <- D |> filter(la == !!la)
  cat(sprintf("- **%s:** %s.\n", la, and_list(d$md)))
}
```

A district is not a local authority. Its schools take their county's
effect on the national models, and what is particular to a district
shows up in its schools' own residuals and in the district test
(@sec-effects).

# The districts side by side

```{r tbl-profile}
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("The twelve districts, ", latest_lab, ". Means of school-level figures. Ranks (1 = highest; for the gap, 1 = widest) are among the ", n_rank, " districts in England with five or more schools; ", and_list(TAB$lad[TAB$schools < 5]), ", with fewer, are each placed among them. Value added is the mean of each school's over 2021/22 to 2024/25.")
TAB |>
  arrange(desc(att8)) |>
  transmute(District = link, County = la, Schools = schools,
            `FSM %` = round(fsm, 1),
            `Att 8` = sprintf("%.1f (%s)", att8, ord(r_att8)),
            `Att 8 disadv.` = sprintf("%.1f (%s)", att8_dis, ord(r_dis)),
            Gap = sprintf("%.1f (%s)", gap, ord(r_gap)),
            `Value added` = sprintf("%+.1f", va),
            `Schools below expectation` = paste(below, "of", schools)) |>
  kt(align = "llrrrrrrl", escape = FALSE)
```

```{r fig-gap}
#| fig-cap: !expr paste0("Attainment 8 for disadvantaged and non-disadvantaged pupils in each district, ", latest_lab, ", school means, with the gap between them. The dotted line is England's average for disadvantaged pupils.")
#| fig-height: 6
TAB |>
  left_join(prof |> select(lad, att8_non), by = "lad") |>
  mutate(lad = reorder(lad, att8_non)) |>
  ggplot(aes(y = lad)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = att8_dis, xend = att8_non, yend = lad), colour = LIGHT, linewidth = 2) +
  geom_point(aes(x = att8_dis, colour = "Disadvantaged"), size = 3.4) +
  geom_point(aes(x = att8_non, colour = "Non-disadvantaged"), size = 3.4) +
  geom_text(aes(x = (att8_dis + att8_non) / 2, label = sprintf("%.1f", gap)),
            vjust = -0.9, size = 3, colour = GREY) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = NAT$att8_dis, linetype = "dotted", colour = PURPLE) +
  facet_grid(la ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Disadvantaged = WARM, `Non-disadvantaged` = TEAL), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Attainment 8", y = NULL,
       title = "The best-performing districts have some of the widest gaps") +
  theme_note()
```

# What explains each district's results {#sec-decomp}

Each district's gap to England, split into the national model's pieces
as in its own document. The pieces sum to the district's total. "Place"
is the South East's effect plus its county's; "schools" is what the
district's own schools add beyond everything the model accounts for.

```{r fig-decomp-heat}
#| fig-cap: "Why each district's average Attainment 8 differs from England's, all school-years 2021/22 to 2024/25, in approximate Attainment 8 points. Red pulls a district below England; teal lifts it above."
#| fig-height: 6.5
grp <- c("Absence" = "Absence", "Prior attainment (KS2)" = "Prior attainment",
         "Disadvantage (% FSM)" = "Disadvantage", "English as an additional language" = "Other intake",
         "Admissions (selection)" = "Other", "Segregation (LA)" = "Other",
         "Teacher workforce" = "Other", "Ofsted rating" = "Ofsted", "Region" = "Place",
         "Local authority effect" = "Place", "Year mix" = "Other",
         "Unexplained (school residual)" = "Schools")
hd <- dec |>
  filter(group %in% c("All pupils", "Disadvantaged")) |>
  mutate(piece = factor(grp[component], c("Absence", "Prior attainment", "Disadvantage",
                                          "Other intake", "Ofsted", "Place", "Other", "Schools"))) |>
  group_by(la, group, piece) |> summarise(points = sum(points), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(la, group) |> mutate(total = sum(points)) |> ungroup()
tots <- hd |> distinct(la, group, total) |> mutate(piece = "Total")
bind_rows(hd, tots |> rename(points = total) |> mutate(total = points)) |>
  mutate(piece = factor(piece, c(levels(hd$piece), "Total")),
         la = factor(la, TAB$lad[order(TAB$att8)])) |>
  ggplot(aes(piece, la, fill = points)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%+.1f", points), fontface = ifelse(piece == "Total", "bold", "plain")),
            size = 2.9, colour = INK) +
  facet_wrap(~group) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = BAD, mid = "#f4f4f7", high = TEAL, midpoint = 0, limits = c(-5, 5),
                       oob = scales::squish, name = "Points") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Different districts, different reasons") +
  theme_note(10) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1), panel.grid = element_blank())
```

```{r decomp-notes}
#| include: false
ab <- sapply(TAB$lad, d_get, g = "All pupils", comp = "Absence")
ks <- sapply(TAB$lad, d_get, g = "All pupils", comp = "Prior attainment (KS2)")
```

Three things stand out:

- **Absence** costs most in `r and_list(names(sort(ab))[1:2])`
  (`r and_list(sgn(sort(ab)[1:2]))` points for all pupils), and lifts
  `r and_list(names(sort(ab, decreasing = TRUE))[1:2])`.
- **Prior attainment** costs most in
  `r and_list(names(sort(ks))[1:2])`.
- **The districts' own schools** add most for all pupils in
  `r and_list(TAB$lad[order(-TAB$u_all)][1:2])`, and take most in
  `r and_list(TAB$lad[order(TAB$u_all)][1:2])`. For disadvantaged pupils
  they take most in `r and_list(TAB$lad[order(TAB$u_dis)][1:2])`.

# Is there a district effect? {#sec-effects}

The district test adds a district level to the national model (see the
[East Sussex document](east_sussex.html#sec-districts)), with and without
each school's own record. An effect that disappears once schools are
counted belongs to particular schools; one that survives is something
the district's schools share.

```{r fig-effects}
#| fig-cap: "District effects over and above each county's, with 95% intervals, on the published specification and with a school term."
#| fig-height: 7
fe |>
  filter(outcome != "Non-disadvantaged") |>
  mutate(spec = factor(spec, c("Published specification", "With a school term")),
         outcome = factor(outcome, c("All pupils", "Disadvantaged", "Absence (stage 1)")),
         lad = factor(lad, rev(sort(unique(lad))))) |>
  ggplot(aes(pct(effect), lad, colour = spec)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = GREY) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = pct(ci_lo), xmax = pct(ci_hi)), height = 0,
                 position = position_dodge(width = 0.6), linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.6), size = 2.4) +
  facet_grid(la ~ outcome, scales = "free", space = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(WARM, TEAL), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "District effect, %", y = NULL, title = "Most district effects vanish once schools are counted") +
  theme_note(10)
```

```{r effects-list}
#| results: asis
for (l in TAB$lad) {
  p <- sig_txt(l, "Published specification"); s <- sig_txt(l, "With a school term")
  if (length(p)) cat(sprintf("- **%s:** %s on the published model; %s.\n", l, and_list(p),
    if (length(s)) paste("with a school term,", and_list(s), "remains") else "none survives a school term"))
}
```

Every other district has no effect distinguishable from zero on either
specification.

# Absence and practice

```{r tbl-absence}
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Absence and practice by district. Overall absence, autumn and spring ", yr(abs_prev), " and ", yr(abs_last), "; absence above or below what the schools' intakes predict, mean 2021/22 to 2024/25; illness and reduced timetables as a percentage of sessions, ", yr(abs_last), "; suspensions per 100 pupils, ", yr(ex_last), ".")
bind_rows(
  TAB |> arrange(la, desc(abs_now)) |>
    transmute(District = link, County = la,
              a1 = abs_before, a2 = abs_now, ex = excess, ill = illness, red = reduced, sus = susp),
  tibble(District = "England", County = "",
         a1 = s_at("England", abs_prev), a2 = s_at("England", abs_last), ex = NA,
         ill = r_at("England", "Illness"), red = r_at("England", "Reduced timetable"),
         sus = ex_at("England"))) |>
  transmute(District, County,
            !!paste("Absence", yr(abs_prev)) := sprintf("%.1f", a1),
            !!paste("Absence", yr(abs_last)) := sprintf("%.1f", a2),
            `Above intake` = ifelse(is.na(ex), "", sprintf("%+.1f", ex)),
            Illness = sprintf("%.2f", ill), `Reduced timetable` = sprintf("%.2f", red),
            `Suspensions per 100` = sprintf("%.1f", sus)) |>
  kt(align = "llrrrrrr", escape = FALSE)
```

```{r fig-abs-series}
#| fig-cap: "Overall absence, autumn and spring terms, 2016/17 to 2025/26, by district, with the county and England. Sessions-weighted; 2019/20 not collected."
#| fig-height: 6
ser |>
  filter(area %in% c(D$lad, "England")) |>
  mutate(la = D$la[match(area, D$lad)], year = yr(time_period)) |>
  (\(d) bind_rows(d |> filter(area != "England"),
                  d |> filter(area == "England") |> select(-la) |>
                    tidyr::crossing(la = names(DISTRICTS))))() |>
  ggplot(aes(year, abs_rate, group = area,
             colour = ifelse(area == "England", "England", "District"))) +
  geom_line(aes(linewidth = area == "England")) +
  geom_text_repel(data = \(d) d |> filter(time_period == abs_last, area != "England"),
                  aes(label = area), size = 2.6, nudge_x = 0.6, direction = "y",
                  hjust = 0, segment.colour = LIGHT, colour = GREY) +
  facet_wrap(~la) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(England = INK, District = TEAL), guide = "none") +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 1.2, `FALSE` = 0.6), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(0.5, 3))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Overall absence, % of sessions",
       title = "Absence rose everywhere after the pandemic and is falling") +
  theme_note(10) + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

# District by district {#sec-each}

Two or three lines on each district, from its own document.

```{r each}
#| results: asis
for (la in names(DISTRICTS)) {
  cat("\n##", la, "\n\n")
  for (l in DISTRICTS[[la]]) {
    t <- TAB |> filter(lad == l)
    p <- sig_txt(l, "Published specification"); s <- sig_txt(l, "With a school term")
    # what the schools add or take, with "about what is expected" near zero
    at <- function(u, who) if (abs(u) < 0.05) paste("do about what is expected for", who)
      else sprintf("%s %.1f points for %s", ifelse(u > 0, "add", "take"), abs(u), who)
    cat(sprintf(paste0(
      "**%s** (%d schools). Attainment 8 %.1f, %s of %d districts; disadvantaged pupils %.1f ",
      "(%s) on %.0f%% disadvantage. Its schools %s and %s beyond what the model expects. ",
      "Absence %.1f%% in %s, %s; suspensions %.1f per 100. %s [Read the %s document](%s).\n\n"),
      l, t$schools, t$att8, ord(t$r_att8), district_rank(SX$lad_profiles, latest, l, "att8")$n,
      t$att8_dis, ord(t$r_dis), t$fsm,
      at(t$u_all, "all pupils"), at(t$u_dis, "disadvantaged pupils"),
      t$abs_now, yr(abs_last),
      if (abs(t$excess) < 0.05) "in line with what the intake predicts over 2021/22 to 2024/25"
      else sprintf("%s what the intake predicts over 2021/22 to 2024/25 by %.1f points",
                   ifelse(t$excess > 0, "above", "below"), abs(t$excess)),
      t$susp,
      if (length(s)) paste0("A district effect survives each school's own record for ", and_list(s), ".")
      else if (length(p)) "A district effect on the published model disappears once each school's record is counted."
      else "No district effect.",
      l, t$doc))
  }
}
```

# Notes on method {.unnumbered}

Methods and sources are those of the [East Sussex](east_sussex.html)
document. District membership comes from each school's postcode (ONS
postcode directory, via postcodes.io). Each district's figures are read
from its own data file (`data/area_<district>.rds`), built by
`R/17_area_analysis.R`; the district effects come from
`R/18_district_effects.R`. This summary is `sussex_districts.qmd`,
rendered by `R/20_district_reports.R` with the district documents. The
format of every tier is described in `AREA_REPORTS.md`.
